The statement says: "there exists a real number $y$ such that, for every real number $x$, $y$ is greater than $x$." In logical notation, this is $\exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \forall x \in \mathbb{R} (y > x)$.

To determine if this is true, we check if there is a real number $y$ that acts as an upper bound for the entire set of real numbers. For any chosen real number $y$, we can always define another real number $x = y + 1$. Since $y + 1 > y$, it is not true that $y > x$ for this specific $x$. Thus, no such $y$ exists because the set of real numbers is unbounded.

The statement is therefore false.
